clue.text: Holy man had us in fits

indicators.note: something in fits is thrown about in spasms, so these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A guru collapses laughing at something the speaker and friends said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fits' rearranges HADUS (from 'had us') into the answer; 'in fits' looks like laughter, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu ascetic or wandering mystic is a holy man.

clue.text: Make leper such a grave

indicators.note: make tells us to form a new word from these letters, an anagram

explanation.surface: Turn a leprosy sufferer into such a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' rearranges LEPERSUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb cut in rock or built for burial is a sepulchre, a grave.

clue.text: Shoots game

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means moves or shoots swiftly
the pub game of throwing feathered arrows at a board

explanation.surface: A game of shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' is a verb meaning dashes, not firing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoots in the sense of speeding along is a synonym, and the arrow-throwing pub contest is a popular game.

clue.text: A flasher in the aisle?

parts.note: flasher suggests an indecent exposer, but it means someone who flashes a torch along a cinema aisle

explanation.surface: An indecent exposer at large in the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: Cinema attendants once showed patrons to their seats with a torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who shows patrons to seats in a cinema or theatre, torch in hand.

clue.text: Carve up underworld clubman

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a man belonging to a club is a member

explanation.surface: A gangland figure from the underworld does some carving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests gangsters, but it is Dis, the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut a body into pieces, i.e. carve it up limb from limb.

clue.text: Bureau has the best sort of computer

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk
top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: An office has the finest kind of computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bureau' suggests an office but is the piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal computer sized to sit on an office table is the desktop kind.

clue.text: Very little weight in this suspicion

definitions.meaning: an apothecaries' unit of twenty grains
a doubt or hesitation on grounds of conscience

explanation.surface: A hint of doubt carrying hardly any weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The apothecaries' measure is old-fashioned: twenty grains, about 1.3 grams.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny pharmacist's unit and a qualm of conscience share the name, the latter a small doubt or suspicion.

clue.text: Run out of pictures for mounting

parts.note: ex means out of, as in ex-directory

indicators.note: in a down clue mounting means rising, so the word for pictures is read upwards

parts.note: art means pictures, paintings

explanation.surface: Having no more photographs ready to frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for mounting' turns ART upwards to TRA; 'mounting' suggests framing pictures. In cricket a run not scored off the bat is an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run added to the total without being hit, called an extra.

clue.text: A capital comforter on the battlefield

definitions.meaning: capital means of the head: a knitted woollen hood worn over the head and neck
the 1854 Crimean War battle, site of the Charge of the Light Brigade

explanation.surface: A cosy item worn during a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means of the head, and a comforter is a woollen scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: The woollen helmet takes its name from the Crimean battle where British troops wore such headgear against the cold.

clue.text: Climber in upright position on flight

definitions.meaning: the vertical board between two treads of a staircase

explanation.surface: A mountaineer standing straight on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gets up or ascends rises, and a staircase's vertical boards are given the same name.

clue.text: Buyer has leverage with supplier in the end

parts.note: purchase is a firm grip giving mechanical advantage, i.e. leverage

indicators.note: the end of the word supplier is its final letter

explanation.surface: A customer has bargaining power with a vendor eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leverage' reads as negotiating clout but means a mechanical grip; 'in the end' picks the last letter of 'supplier'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who buys goods is a buyer, the opposite of a seller.

clue.text: Hoffman's might be prayed for

definitions.meaning: Offenbach's opera is known as the ... of Hoffmann
a writ summoning bystanders to fill up a jury, which counsel may pray for

explanation.surface: Something about Hoffman that one might pray to obtain.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal writ is obscure: when a jury panel ran short, a party would 'pray a tales' to have bystanders sworn in.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenbach's opera title pairs stories with Hoffmann, and a writ to complete a jury bears the same Latin-derived name.

clue.text: One of the weepers who has been beaten

explanation.surface: A mourner who has also taken a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half alludes to the children's saying 'finders keepers, losers weepers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground rhyme casts those who lose things as weepers, and the defeated party in any contest is the one that lost.

clue.text: You can hear his patter on the boards

definitions.text: You can hear his patter on the boards

parts.words: You can hear his patter on the boards
parts.note: patter reads as an actor's stage chatter, but it is the patter of metal-tipped shoes on stage floorboards

explanation.surface: A stage performer whose chat carries to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patter' suggests talk; here it is the sound of feet, and 'the boards' is the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in metal-plated shoes makes a rhythmic tapping, the patter heard on stage.

clue.text: Chap who will, say, drain what's left in glass

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving a sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a chap who will is 'he will', contracted to he'll
to tap a cask is to draw off or drain its liquid

explanation.surface: A man resolves to empty whatever remains in his glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns HE'LL ('Chap who will') into its sound-alike HEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the dregs or small amount of liquor left in the bottom of a glass.

clue.text: Style Anne adapted for novel

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anne's writing manner is altered for a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges STYLEANNE. Mrs Henry Wood's 1861 Victorian bestseller was famously adapted for stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Henry Wood's sensational 1861 melodrama is a Victorian novel.

clue.text: Few men remain for this last bit of the match

definitions.meaning: the closing stage of a chess game, when only a few pieces are left on the board
the final phase of any contest

explanation.surface: Late in a game, when only a few players are left standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men' are chess pieces, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the phase when most pieces have been exchanged is the closing stage, and figuratively any contest's final phase.

clue.text: Import teak, say, as main material

definitions.text: Import teak, say, as main material

parts.words: Import teak, say, as main material
parts.note: main reads as chief but means the sea: timber such as teak brought ashore by the waves

explanation.surface: Bringing in tropical hardwood as the principal building stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea, not chief, and the import is washed ashore rather than shipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber washed up on a beach after floating on the sea is driftwood.

clue.text: Duck below the duvet

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck prized for its soft feathers
down means below

explanation.surface: Diving under the quilt to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' reads as a verb, to dodge, but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with soft feathers, originally those of the sea duck, is a duvet.

clue.text: Record by US writer and sculptor

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
Gertrude Stein was an American writer

explanation.surface: A recording of an American author who also sculpts.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor; 'by' just places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a celebrated twentieth-century sculptor working in bronze and stone.

clue.text: Nothing to do with the organ of a large flower

parts.note: nil means nothing
otic means relating to the ear, an organ

explanation.surface: Nothing connected with a big bloom's reproductive parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a river: here the Nile, Africa's great river.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the Nile, a great river or flowing thing.

clue.text: A pirate ship, moreover

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
and means also, moreover

explanation.surface: A buccaneer, and a vessel besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A pirate ship' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'pirate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit or outlaw who plunders is a brigand, close kin to a pirate.

clue.text: Bombardment from ship borne gunners

indicators.note: borne means carried, so the barge carries the gunners inside it

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed vessel
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A shelling from artillerymen carried aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borne' is the container signal; in the surface 'ship-borne' reads as one compound adjective, hiding that the ship carries the gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy continuous artillery attack is a barrage, a sustained bombardment.

clue.text: Spy a copper god of such weight

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a Lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A spy, a policeman and a deity all of considerable weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal's symbol; Lares were Roman household gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecular weight is the mass of a molecule, so the word describes that kind of weight.

clue.text: Current styles the mannequins left out

indicators.note: out signals the abbreviation is removed from the word

parts.note: models are mannequins, those who display clothes

explanation.surface: This season's fashions that the catwalk models didn't wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like one phrase meaning omitted, but 'left' is L and 'out' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashions or ways of doing things are modes, current styles.

clue.text: A sign of something missing — a' litre of the red wine?

definitions.text: A sign of something missing — a' litre of the red wine?

indicators.note: something missing has been removed, so a letter is taken out of the wine

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A mark showing that a litre of red has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes L (litre) out of CLARET; the whole clue is both definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's mark showing where an omission should be inserted, an inverted V placed below a line.

clue.text: Democrat in defeat retired from the House

indicators.note: something that has retired has gone back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
in places the abbreviation inside the word for defeat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A Democrat beaten in an election leaves the House of Representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside ROUT to give RODUT, and 'retired' turns that round. 'the House' is not Congress but a royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were an English royal dynasty, and a dynasty is called a house.

clue.text: Information given in notice put up by corporation

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means raised, so the word for notice is read upwards

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
corporation is old slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: Details published in an announcement posted by the council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns AD into DA. 'corporation' reads as a council or company, but is a jocular word for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item of fact taken as known, a piece of data, is a datum.

clue.text: Benefactor's name is in the entrance

definitions.note: read as 'benefactor is', a noun the answer matches

indicators.note: is in tells us the abbreviation sits inside the word for the entrance

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A patron's name is displayed by the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Benefactor's' is the definition plus 'is'; patrons' names are often shown at a building's door.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gives money or blood is a giver, a benefactor.

clue.text: Cha-cha tune?

parts.note: cha is slang for a cup of char, and two of them make a famous song title for two people taking a cuppa

explanation.surface: A piece of music for a Latin dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (char) is British slang for tea, so 'Cha-cha' is two teas; the clue looks like a dance-tune request.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1925 song from No, No, Nanette is a tune, and cha-cha doubles the slang word for a cuppa.

clue.text: Places, etc, where you may find a public display

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are found rearranged in the answer, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Locations and so on where a show might be staged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where you may find' is a loose anagram signal working on PLACESETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A striking show or pageant put on for the public is a spectacle.

clue.text: Second dan holder is a loyal friend

indicators.note: dan is the holder, containing the word for a second

parts.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A black belt in judo of second dan proves a faithful companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second dan' reads as a martial-arts grade, but 'holder' makes dan the container for the word meaning a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Damon offered his life for his friend Pythias, so his name stands for loyal friendship.
